The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Ethics, Privileges and Public Petitions, Senator Neda Imasuen, has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos on their historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, describing it as a landmark achievement for Nigeria and African football. Imasuen, who represents Edo South Senatorial District, praised the players for their resilience, determination and fighting spirit, which propelled them to become the first African nation to win the competition. In a congratulatory statement issued through his media aide, Moshood Karim, and made available to journalists in Abuja, the senator said the team’s journey from an opening-day defeat to six consecutive victories before lifting the trophy demonstrated their character, discipline and belief. The Flamingos made history on Saturday in Morocco after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final to claim the 2026 title. Imasuen said the triumph had brought immense pride to Nigeria while breaking new ground for African women’s football on the global stage. He added that the achievement should inspire aspiring female footballers across the country, particularly young girls seeking to represent Nigeria at the highest level. The lawmaker urged the Federal Government, football administrators and other stakeholders to sustain investment in grassroots sports development, especially women’s football, to identify, nurture and support more talents capable of achieving success internationally. He also expressed confidence in the potential of Nigerian youths, saying the Flamingos had demonstrated that determination, adequate support and opportunities could help them compete and succeed on the world stage. “Nigeria is proud of the Flamingos. Africa is proud of the Flamingos. Their historic victory has opened a new chapter in African women’s football,” he said. Kindly share this story:
